Adding another data point, because I likely hit related Windows install-state symptoms as well.

On my machine I found historical OpenCode footprints under both:

* `%LocalAppData%\Programs\OpenCode`
* `%LocalAppData%\OpenCode`

The updater cache also still contained:

* `%LocalAppData%\@opencode-aidesktop-updater\pending\opencode-desktop-win-x64.exe`

In my case the immediate user-visible problem was that the app was stranded on `v1.16.2` because automatic startup/periodic update checks did not run. That appears to be a separate updater lifecycle regression likely fixed by #31191, so I filed it separately.

But the duplicate/wrong-location install history here looks related to this issue and the other reports in #30497 / #32690.

The introducing config change for the install-location behavior seems to be #26253:

* before: `oneClick: false` plus `allowToChangeInstallationDirectory: true`
* after: `oneClick: true` plus `perMachine: false`
* `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()` also changed to `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall(true, true)`

That PR was first included in `v1.14.42`. `v1.14.41` still had the assisted/custom-directory installer config, while current `v1.17.16` still appears to use `oneClick: true` and `perMachine: false`.

So I think there are two distinct Windows updater issues that can be confused:

* duplicate/wrong-location installs after the one-click per-user installer change, tracked here
* automatic update checks not running in `v1.16.2`, apparently fixed by #31191

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

Ran into the same `Provider.list` TypeError while debugging a plugin and can
offer a root-cause hypothesis plus a way to check it.

The only dereference in the `Provider.list` path that can produce
`undefined is not an object (evaluating '….provider')` is the plugin hooks
loop in the Provider state build (`provider/provider.ts:1372`, `const p =
hook.provider`): the guard `if (!p || !models) continue` sits one line *after*
the deref, so it protects against a hook without a provider, but not against a
falsy hooks-array entry. Such entries can get in because `applyPlugin`
(`plugin/index.ts`) pushes plugin results unchecked — e.g. any *function*
export on a legacy-shaped plugin module is called as a plugin, and a helper
export's `undefined` return lands in the hooks array. The `plugin config hook
failed … (evaluating '….config')` line that tends to precede the 500 is the
same phantom entry hitting the config-notify loop.

On "happens with all plugins removed": OpenCode also auto-discovers file-based
plugins — `config/plugin.ts` globs `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}` in every
config directory (project `.opencode/`, global config dir, etc.) — so plugins
can load even with an empty `plugin` array. Could you check:

1. the contents of `~/.config/opencode/plugin/` and `plugins/` (and any
   project-local `.opencode/plugin*/` dirs in the workspace you had open), and
2. which config files OpenCode is merging for you (any leftover file-based
   plugin in a directory you'd forgotten counts)?

If a `.ts`/`.js` file shows up there, its module shape (specifically: extra
function exports, or a `server()` that can resolve `undefined`) would explain
the crash exactly. I've opened #36102 which makes the loader skip falsy
hook returns and log a warning naming the offending plugin spec — with that
patch this failure mode becomes a log line instead of a dead instance.

## Additional report (macOS 26.5, opencode 1.17.17)

Hit the same blank TUI on a fresh Homebrew install (`anomalyco/tap/opencode` 1.17.17).

### Environment
- **OS:** macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64)
- **Install:** Homebrew (`/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode`)
- **Terminal:** standard macOS terminal (also reproducible in non-TTY environments)

### Symptoms
- Running `opencode` → blank screen, no UI, appears hung
- `opencode run` and TUI mode hang at `init` in logs
- `opencode serve` starts fine (headless works)
- `opencode models`, `opencode debug config` work without full instance init

### `~/Library` size
- **~45 GB** and **~650k files** when the bug occurred
- After cleanup (removed Android SDK, unused app data, etc.) still **~27 GB** — issue was present before and after cleanup

### Logs
Logs stop at `init`, then (when run with a PTY) `ENAMETOOLONG: name too long, open` during directory walk — consistent with file watcher / home-dir scanning blocking startup.

### Workaround (confirmed working)
Launch with a minimal `HOME` and symlink real config/data paths:

```bash
REAL_HOME="$HOME"
MINIMAL_HOME="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/opencode-minimal-home-${USER}"
mkdir -p "$MINIMAL_HOME"/{.config,.local/share,.local/state,.cache}
ln -sf "$REAL_HOME/.config/opencode" "$MINIMAL_HOME/.config/opencode"
ln -sf "$REAL_HOME/.local/share/opencode" "$MINIMAL_HOME/.local/share/opencode"
ln -sf "$REAL_HOME/.local/state/opencode" "$MINIMAL_HOME/.local/state/opencode"
ln -sf "$REAL_HOME/.cache/opencode" "$MINIMAL_HOME/.cache/opencode"
export HOME="$MINIMAL_HOME"
exec /opt/homebrew/bin/opencode "$@"
```

With this wrapper, TUI starts normally and `opencode run` completes successfully.

### What did NOT help
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=1`
- `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER=true`
- Clearing `~/.cache/opencode` and `~/.local/share/opencode`
- `--pure` flag

Implemented in #36105 (merged to `v2` as `6524dfc818`).

The managed server now suspends its active Sessions on graceful shutdown (private `session.time_suspended` timestamp) and the next managed server resumes each suspended Session at most once, consuming the suspension atomically before the drain starts. Default, embedded, and stdio servers never suspend or auto-resume. Hard-crash recovery stays out of scope and is tracked by #35642.

Design notes live in `specs/v2/session-restart-continuation.md`.

If your issue is specifically about the `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` model name being invalid on Prima Labs as the routing backend (rather than a general big-pickle outage), it may be worth noting that distinction in those threads or confirming whether this is a new/separate regression.

The issue is in packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts — when a file is attached, the filename field is set to whatever path string was used

This gets passed through message-v2.ts into the AI SDK's convertToModelMessages(), which then sends it to the Anthropic/Bedrock API as the document name. The API rejects filenames containing / characters.

The fix would be a one-liner in prompt.ts to use path.basename(filename) instead of the full path when setting the filename field on file parts.

## Diagnostic from opencode/big-pickle logs (v1.17.16, Linux Ubuntu 24.04)

### Config
```json
{ "model": "opencode/big-pickle" }
```

### Error timeline for big-pickle (Jun 11 – Jul 9)

| Error | Frequency | Period |
|---|---|---|
| Rate limit exceeded | 60+ occurrences | Jun 11 – Jul 9 |
| Socket connection closed | 20+ | Jun 21 |
| **Prima Labs: Invalid model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`** | **8** | **Jul 9 (today)** |
| Internal Server Error | 4 | Jun 24 |
| Service Unavailable | 2 | Jun 23, Jul 4 |
| Cannot connect to API | 10+ | Jun 13, Jun 23 |
| Insufficient Balance | 2 | Jul 3 |

### 🔍 New diagnostic: exact root cause from Jul 9 logs

The Prima Labs error started **today** and provides the exact model routing:

```
AI_APICallError: Error from provider (Prima Labs): /chat/completions:
Invalid model name passed in model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
Call `/v1/models` to view available models for your key.
```

The OpenCode routing sends `opencode/big-pickle` → Prima Labs provider with model name `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, which does **not exist** on Prima Labs' API.

### Key differences from #28138

| | #28138 (May 18) | Our logs (Jul 9) |
|---|---|---|
| Error | "Model big-pickle not supported for format anthropic" | "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash not a valid model on Prima Labs" |
| Nature | Format mapping bug | Invalid model name on upstream provider |

This could be:
1. A new routing configuration pushing big-pickle through Prima Labs with the wrong model name
2. Prima Labs dropping/deprecating that model
3. A regression in the routing layer post internal refactor

Suggest checking whether `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` is still a valid model on Prima Labs (call `/v1/models`) and whether the routing should be updated to a valid model or a different provider.
